facts.fact: The plan states that the National Registration Bureau, a department under the Ministry of Homeland Security, is the central body responsible for civil registration and maintains the NRIS, working through District Registration Offices under the District Commissioner as District Registrar; no date is given, so the plan's published date is used.
facts.system: CRVS system (CRVS subsystem of the NRIS)

facts.fact: The plan states that significant reliance on CDC and its partner EGPAF for maintaining the CRVS system is a high risk, and its assessment table names NRB and EGPAF as the parties to the eCRVS system and database; no date is given, so the plan's published date is used.
facts.system: CRVS system (CRVS subsystem of the NRIS)

facts.fact: The NRB Strategic Plan 2025-2030 makes civil registration its first key result area, costed at MWK 66.06 billion over 2025-26 to 2029-30, with targets of birth and death registration in 595 health facilities, 415 functional Traditional Authority offices and 96 post offices, and full digitalisation of the CRVS system.
facts.system: CRVS system (CRVS subsystem of the NRIS)

facts.fact: The plan states that donor engagement has been a key driver of CRVS improvements while limited domestic budget allocations threaten the sustainability and expansion of services, naming CDC, UNICEF, UNDP, EGPAF and the World Bank as providers of financing and technical assistance; no date is given, so the plan's published date is used.
facts.system: CRVS system (CRVS subsystem of the NRIS)

facts.fact: The plan states that CRVS kits at district registration offices register births and deaths and print certificates, that death registration was started through a decentralised electronic module under the NRIS, and that eBirth and eDeath registration exist in the country; no date is given, so the plan's published date is used.
facts.system: CRVS system (CRVS subsystem of the NRIS)

facts.fact: The plan states that CRVS registration kits at district and registration offices register births and deaths and synchronise data with the NRIS central system over the government wide area network or TNM mobile links, and that health facilities now register births on site in maternity wards; no date is given, so the plan's published date is used.
facts.system: CRVS system (CRVS subsystem of the NRIS)

facts.fact: The plan's review of 2019-2024 states that in some remote areas the digital birth registration system had not fully replaced paper, with data gaps where forms from community registrars and hospitals were lost or not entered centrally, and that unstable connectivity at many district offices and health facilities delayed synchronising of registrations.
facts.system: CRVS system (CRVS subsystem of the NRIS)

facts.fact: The plan (NRB) counts among its achievements the digitisation of 142 high-volume health centres for birth and death registration, gives no total of registering sites, sets a target of 595 health facilities by 2030 and says the number of CRVS kits is limited; no date is given, so the plan's published date is used.
facts.system: CRVS system (CRVS subsystem of the NRIS)
